geographic_notes.text: The CCDR's regional indicator shows different hazard-risk patterns in Praslin/La Digue and the West region under moderate and rare severe events. Its table and prose use different population/household labels, so precise percentages are not carried forward.
Source dated 2026-03 reports: About 48% of roads on Mahé, Praslin and La Digue are exposed to coastal erosion/flooding; a 2023 SLTA study flags Bel Ombre, Port Glaud, Au Cap and L’Amitié Road.
Source dated 2023-12 reports: At four Mahé zones and Praslin/La Digue, TNC projects little mean-annual rainfall change but 4–8 additional extreme wet days per year from a two-day historical average.

Source dated 2023-12 reports: TNC identifies Anse Kerlan (north-west Praslin) and Anse Royale (south-east Mahé) among eroded, vulnerable beaches, citing steep reef bathymetry that lets waves break close to shore.
